conventions.convention: The time factor is exp(−iωt), outgoing spherical modes use exp(+ikr), and the exterior spherical model has a>0, k>0, smooth boundary data and the uniform Sommerfeld condition.
The Cartesian stretch is X=x+iS with S(x)=∫₀ˣσ(t)dt and s=1+iσ; σ is nonnegative, continuous, piecewise C¹ and zero for x≤0. The normal operator is s⁻¹∂x(s⁻¹∂x).
The local impedance condition is ∂nu−iku=0 with the outward normal; at the artificial plane x=R that normal is +ex.
Spherical harmonic degree starts at ℓ=0; unit-sphere surface measure has mass 4π and the L² inner product is linear in its first argument.
The exact DtN symbol is τℓ(k,R)=k hℓ′(kR)/hℓ(kR), using the outgoing first-kind spherical Hankel function and the increasing-r radial derivative.
For 0<a<R, the modal energy weights are r² on radial derivatives and 1+ℓ(ℓ+1) on values. Tests have zero inner trace, and the variational form subtracts R² times the outer DtN pairing.
Propagating-mode attenuation assumes real q>0; uniform decay requires q≥q₀>0. Grazing behavior is a limit, and the theorem supplies no evanescent attenuation assertion.

load_bearing.statement: For integers ℓ≥0 and real z>0, |hℓ(z)|²=Σₘ₌₀^ℓ Sℓm z^(−2m−2), where Sℓm=(2m)!(ℓ+m)!/[4^m(m!)²(ℓ−m)!]. Consequently |hℓ(z)| is nonincreasing in z, |hℓ₋₁(z)|≤|hℓ(z)| for ℓ≥1, and |hℓ′(z)|≤(1+(ℓ+1)/z)|hℓ(z)|. For fixed z₀>0 and all z≥z₀, |z(hℓ′(z)−ihℓ(z))|/|hℓ(z₀)|≤(ℓ+1)e^(2z₀).

For every k,R>0 and smooth g on S², the defining DtN series converges in C∞ and |τℓ(k,R)|≤k+(ℓ+1)/R. Its outgoing extension converges in C² on each compact annulus R≤r≤R₁, solves Helmholtz, has trace g and radial derivative Tₖ,ᴿg at R, satisfies the uniform Sommerfeld condition, and is the unique classical outgoing extension of g.

For fixed 0<a<R and k>0 there is C=C(a,R,k) such that every u,v in the coefficient energy space satisfy Σℓ≥0(1+ℓ)(‖uℓ(a)‖₂²+‖uℓ(R)‖₂²)≤C‖u‖V² and |aₖ,ₐ,ᴿ(u,v)|≤C‖u‖V‖v‖V. The space is a Hilbert direct sum and finite-degree truncations converge in its norm.

For k>0, η∈R² with |η|<k and q=√(k²−|η|²)>0, exp(iqX(x)+iη·y) solves the pulled-back Helmholtz equation, matches the physical mode's value and scaled normal flux at x=0, and has modulus exp(−qS(x)). Families with q≥q₀>0 satisfy the stated uniform attenuation bounds; no uniform bound is asserted as q decreases to zero.

For 0<q≤k and q²+|η|²=k², the stated incident-plus-reflected plane wave satisfies the local impedance condition exactly when its reflection coefficient is (q−k)/(q+k). Its magnitude is (k−q)/(k+q), zero at normal incidence and tending to one at grazing incidence.
For q>0, A≠0 and a finite stretched layer with S(L)>0, imposing u(L)=0 on u=A exp(iqX)+B exp(−iqX) gives B/A=−exp(2iqX(L)) and |B/A|=exp(−2qS(L)).
For a>0, k>0 and the exterior-model convention, every classical outgoing solution of (Δ+k²)u=0 on r>a with zero Dirichlet trace at r=a is identically zero.

seams_checked.note: Read both page texts and the four BEM-homed exterior-model, angular, radial-flux and outgoing-mode foundations. Their exact positive-frequency, outgoing and harmonic-normalization interfaces support the PE18 uses. In the reverse direction, the BEM general-obstacle uniqueness proof uses outgoing projections only outside an enclosing sphere, then Green's identity and unique continuation; it does not use the spherical-obstacle zero-trace theorem for general geometry. The combined-field theorem cites that separate general-obstacle result and explicitly limits its inverse bound to fixed frequency.
